newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian taxi drivers, police block city centre.
newsitem.headline: Serbian taxi drivers, police block city centre.

text.p: Police prevented several thousand taxi drivers from reaching government buildings in central Belgrade on Wednesday to demand tax cuts and a ban on the import of second-hand cars.
The way was blocked by special police units in combat gear but some protesters abandoned their cars and continued on foot amid traffic chaos.
The Serbian minister for private enterprise, Radoje Djukic, told a taxi drivers' rally that their demands were justified.
Milivoj Armus, head of Belgrade's biggest taxi company, said the protest had been postponed for a month after the government promised to deal with their problems.

"But nothing has been done since and we therefore have an additional demand -- that deputy Serbian finance minister Djuradj Novakovic who made these promises resigns," Armus said. "We will continue our protest until our demands are met."
Belgrade drivers were joined by colleagues from towns throughout Serbia in a general strike against high taxes and the import ban.
"High taxes are making it impossible for us to earn a decent living," said a drivers' spokesman said.
Serbia has around 20,000 registered taxi drivers, of whom half are in Belgrade, which has a quarter of Yugoslavia's 11 million population.
High unemployment and low wages have pushed many people, including professionals, into cab driving.
The strike has added to tension in Serbia, which has recently been shaken by a wave of worker protests as the economy worsens.
Traffic on the main bridge to the city centre was blocked during the peak afternoon hours by police and taxi drivers.
